content.doc_md:
Cherry-picklets you copy a single commit from one branch to another. It's useful when you want just one (or a few) changes, not everything from another branch.

Apatchis a file with changes from one or more commits. You can share a patch or apply it to another repository, even if it's unrelated to your own.

Copy a specific commit from another branch to your current branch:

This creates a new commit on your branch with the same changes.

Use--editto change the commit message while cherry-picking:

Use--no-commit(or-n) to apply the changes, but not create a commit yet. This lets you make more changes before committing:

Use-xto add a line to the commit message showing where the commit came from:

Tip:Usecherry-pickfor copying a single commit in the same repository.

Usepatchesto share changes as files or work across repositories.

If you want to keep commit history and authors, usegit aminstead ofgit apply.

### Code Snippets

```
Example: Cherry-pick a Commit
git cherry-pick abc1234

---

Example: Edit Commit Message
git cherry-pick abc1234 --edit

---

Example: Cherry-pick Without Commit
git cherry-pick abc1234 --no-commit

---

Example: Cherry-pick With Origin
git cherry-pick abc1234 -x

---

Example: Continue After Conflict
git add .
git cherry-pick --continue

---

Example: Abort Cherry-pick
git cherry-pick --abort

---

Example: Create Patch
git format-patch -1 abc1234

---

Example: Multiple Commits
git format-patch HEAD~3

---

Example: Apply Patch
git apply 0001-some-change.patch

---

Example: Apply Patch with Metadata
git am 0001-some-change.patch

---

Example: Reverse Patch
git apply -R 0001-some-change.patch
```
